properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From the hxm_program hub's 2026-09-28 field report (art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28), O-24, in the reporter's words: "A composite orientation read. One `orientation` call returning what where-am-i needs, bounded, so a flaky harness costs one retry, not eight (F-36)."

WHAT THE ROOT-CAUSE PASS FOUND (fact:root-cause-where-am-i-rests-on-fourteen-separate-reads-and-no-skill-says-what-to-answer-when-one-is-refused-2026-09-28): the refusals were the harness's. All seven tools involved publish the same {"readOnlyHint": true}. What reflow2 owns is that where-am-i gathers from 15 read calls over 10 tools and states no minimum answer, and none of the 32 served skills says what to do when a call it names is refused. The reporter's fallback answer worked because graph_report_markdown is already a composite (snapshot, delivery line, top gaps, allocation, maturity).

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) ONE COMPOSITE READ, `orientation`, bounded. Each section (delivery, decisions settled, open questions, what next, stale findings, loop closure, drift from the committed export) is computed independently and returned with its own ok, withheld or error, so a slow or failing section degrades to a note inside one reply.
(b) THE SKILL STATES ITS MINIMUM. graph_report_markdown plus a brief scan of Decisions is the floor, the other reads are enrichments, and the answer says which reads were refused. No new tool. At the class, every served skill that gathers from several calls names its floor.
(c) GROW THE COMPOSITE THAT EXISTS. Add what where-am-i needs and graph_report_markdown lacks (decisions settled, stale findings, loop closure) to it, so the existing composite covers the skill.
(d) NOTHING. The refusal was the harness's, and may not recur.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· LATENCY: the four orientation rollups measured 35 of 40 seconds on 2026-09-05 (fact:the-agent-surface-profiled-orientation-is-35-of-40-seconds-and-two-causes-are-located). Bundled, they make one call of about 30 seconds, and if that one call is refused or times out, everything is lost. That is the reverse of the intent, unless the composite degrades internally as (a) describes.
· FREEZING: where-am-i's gather list moves (Constraint was added 2026-08-24, Contributor and loop closure later). A composite tool freezes the list in code, or must be driven by the skill's own list.
· FEWER THINGS (dec:idea-reflow2-does-fewer-things-and-does-them-really-well): (a) is one more tool on a 193-tool surface. Against that, it could retire the most-repeated fifteen-call sequence an agent runs. (b) adds nothing to the surface.
· dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written (accepted) already says orientation is a projection; (a) and (c) are that projection as a single call, and (b) keeps it as a procedure.
· Building for a transient harness fault is building for something reflow2 does not control. The same floor would also serve a hosted door over a network, and a restarting daemon.
· Size, as information: (a) medium, a new tool with per-section budgets; (b) small, skill text plus a lint; (c) small to medium; (d) none.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 serve ONE bounded orientation read that returns what where-am-i needs, section by section, so a refused or failing call costs one retry instead of fifteen, or should the skill instead name its minimum answer and say which reads were refused?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill (fetched fresh) during the triage of art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28. Searched first ("composite orientation read", "one call where-am-i"): the nearest are the 2026-09-14 project-scoped status rollup (one call instead of a hand assembly, for status), the accepted orientation-is-computed decision, and the topic view; none asks for the where-am-i bundle or a degraded path.
